title: Guidelines in Medicine
coreMove: Treat a structured clinical guideline as the default starting point and require explicit justification for departing from it, rather than treating adherence as optional or guidelines as merely advisory.
sourcePressure: Clinical guidelines reduce some avoidable variation in medical decisions. They work best when they establish the default behavior from which departure requires justification, rather than as a ceiling above which good doctors operate. Guidelines help not by replacing judgment but by making variation in judgment visible and requiring it to be named.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating clinical guidelines as a constraint imposed on expert judgment by administrators or guideline committees, rather than as a consistency anchor that elevates median outcomes across a population of patients.

sourceAnchors.name: Clinical guideline effects on practice variation
sourceAnchors.detail: Research on guideline implementation across sepsis management, antibiotic prescribing, statin therapy, and cancer screening shows that practice variance falls when guidelines are treated as defaults rather than recommendations, and that patient outcomes at the population level improve because the floor is raised even if the ceiling is not.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A clinical guideline does not make every doctor better. It makes the worst outcomes rarer. That is a different claim, and it is the one that matters for population health.

hook: what happens when medicine becomes a formula?
counterintuition: following guidelines makes you a better doctor
the best doctors follow guidelines most of the time
tryThisNow: think of a professional guideline you routinely ignore
notice the next time you depart from standard practice
examples: a scene where the guideline is shown to be wrong in a specific case — the chapter's point is not that guidelines are always right, but that departures should be named; a scene that frames guidelines as bureaucratic obstacles to good medicine

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: Medical guideline examples risk all reading as 'doctor does or doesn't follow protocol with varying results.' Different clinical domains and formats are needed to show how the default-with-named-departure principle applies across different guideline types.

exampleSpecs.domain: sepsis treatment: an ICU measuring whether adherence to the sepsis bundle reduces variation in time-to-antibiotics across physicians
exampleSpecs.audience: an ICU medical director conducting a quality review of sepsis bundle compliance
exampleSpecs.stakes: patient mortality — sepsis is time-critical, and variation in time-to-antibiotics is a direct patient harm driver
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the medical director presents the compliance data: on days when the sepsis bundle was treated as a default (any departure required a documented clinical reason), time-to-antibiotics had a standard deviation of 28 minutes; on days when the bundle was treated as advisory, the standard deviation was 71 minutes — and the average time was also longer on advisory days
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a quality dashboard showing two distributions of time-to-antibiotics: one tighter and centered earlier, one wider and centered later — labeled 'bundle as default' and 'bundle as advisory'
mustInclude: the 28 vs. 71 minute standard deviation comparison
both the variance reduction and the mean improvement
the default-versus-advisory framing as the only operationally different variable
mustAvoid: implying any physician who departed from the bundle was incompetent

exampleSpecs.domain: antibiotic prescribing in primary care: a clinic measuring whether a default-with-justification protocol reduces inappropriate antibiotic use
exampleSpecs.audience: a primary care network quality manager comparing antibiotic prescribing rates before and after protocol introduction
exampleSpecs.stakes: antibiotic stewardship and patient health — inappropriate prescribing varies widely across physicians treating similar presentations and contributes to resistance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager reviews the protocol's first year: inappropriate antibiotic prescribing rate (prescriptions for viral presentations where guidelines recommend watchful waiting) fell from 34 percent to 19 percent after the default protocol was introduced, while the physicians who documented explicit clinical reasons for departing showed only a marginal rate decline — the largest drop came from situations where no justification was easy to write
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a trend chart of inappropriate antibiotic prescribing rate over two years: the line declining sharply at the point the default protocol was introduced
mustInclude: the mechanism: the requirement to name the departure reason is what does the work, not the guideline's content
the marginal decline in justified departures versus the large decline in unjustified ones
mustAvoid: a scene that implies any physician intentionally overprescribed

exampleSpecs.domain: statin prescribing for cardiovascular risk: a cardiology group comparing prescribing variance before and after a structured shared-decision-making protocol
exampleSpecs.audience: a cardiology quality improvement team studying prescribing consistency for guideline-eligible patients
exampleSpecs.stakes: cardiovascular outcomes — guideline-eligible patients who do not receive statins due to physician preference variation have preventable events
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: two cardiologists in a quality review meeting compare their prescribing rates for guideline-eligible patients and find a 28-point difference: one has a 90 percent statin initiation rate for eligible patients, the other 62 percent — and when asked about their decision process, the lower-rate physician describes considering statin benefits versus side effects as an open question, rather than as a question where the guideline has already answered the default
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a prescribing consistency report showing two physicians' statin initiation rates for the same patient population, the gap clearly labeled
mustInclude: the 28-point gap between two physicians with the same patient population
the lower-rate physician's framing of the decision as open when the guideline treats it as a default
the quality team's framing: the problem is not that the lower-rate physician is wrong, but that the departure from guideline default is unnamed and unmeasured
mustAvoid: a scene that implies statins are always the right choice

exampleSpecs.domain: cancer screening referral in primary care: a health system comparing referral rate variance across GPs for the same screening-eligible patient population
exampleSpecs.audience: a primary care network analyzing whether a referral decision-support tool reduces variation
exampleSpecs.stakes: early cancer detection — patients who are not referred for guideline-eligible screening miss early detection opportunities that are later detected at advanced stage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the network director asks the room: for patients who meet every guideline criterion for colorectal cancer screening referral, what is the range of referral rates across our network physicians? The answer from the data is 39 to 97 percent — a 58-point range for patients who according to guidelines should be referred uniformly, with the variation correlating with individual physician beliefs about screening benefit rather than patient characteristics
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a histogram of colorectal cancer referral rates across network physicians for guideline-eligible patients, the bars showing a wide spread from 39 to 97 percent
mustInclude: the correlation with physician belief rather than patient characteristic
the director's framing: guideline eligibility should be the default decision; the variation represents departure without naming
mustAvoid: implying that all 58-point variation is due to physician negligence

exampleSpecs.domain: hypertension management: a hospital system comparing variance in blood-pressure targets across cardiologists treating the same patient population
exampleSpecs.audience: a hospital quality committee reviewing prescribing consistency for antihypertensive therapy targets
exampleSpecs.stakes: long-term patient cardiovascular outcomes — systematic variation in treatment targets leads to population-level differences in stroke and kidney disease incidence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast the pre-protocol period (cardiologists using personal target preferences) with the post-protocol period (guideline BP target as the default, departures documented): prescribing variance for the same patient risk category fell by 45 percent, and the documentation of departures revealed that 80 percent of departures had either sound clinical reasons or were simply habits that had never been examined against the guideline
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a quality review board presentation showing two treatment-target distributions for the same patient population: the pre-protocol distribution wide and bimodal, the post-protocol distribution narrower and centered on the guideline target
mustInclude: the departure documentation revealing 80 percent were either justified or habitual
the habitual-departure finding as the important result: named departures become examined departures
mustAvoid: a stroke or kidney disease outcome story
implying any cardiologist was practicing below standard

exampleSpecs.domain: stroke triage protocol in an emergency department: a hospital comparing door-to-imaging time variance before and after stroke guideline adoption as default
exampleSpecs.audience: an emergency medicine quality officer studying whether guideline adoption reduces variance in time-critical care
exampleSpecs.stakes: stroke outcomes — the treatment window for stroke is time-critical, and variance in time-to-imaging is a direct driver of patient harm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the quality officer reviews the first six months after the stroke triage protocol was adopted as a default: door-to-imaging variance fell from a standard deviation of 24 minutes to 9 minutes; the mean also fell from 38 to 22 minutes; and the three departments that showed the smallest improvement were the ones where the protocol was described to staff as a recommendation rather than a default
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an emergency department time-log comparing the pre-protocol and post-protocol distributions of door-to-imaging times, the post-protocol curve tighter and shifted left
mustInclude: the three lagging departments as evidence that 'recommendation' framing undermines the default effect
mustAvoid: implying the departments that presented the protocol as a recommendation were negligent

skillTargets: explain how the default-with-named-departure framing differs from treating guidelines as recommendations
identify what makes a guideline implementation effective versus ineffective at reducing variation
apply the default-departure logic to a non-medical professional guideline context
analyze why the departure-documentation requirement is often more powerful than the guideline's content in reducing noise
evaluate whether a described guideline implementation would raise the floor on outcomes or only formalize existing practice

tryThisNowSpec: Find one professional standard or guideline that applies to a decision you make regularly. For your next 10 decisions of that type, treat the guideline as the default and write one sentence when you depart from it. At the end of the 10 cases, read the departure sentences. Some will have sound reasons. Some will describe habits you had not examined. Those are the noise the guideline is meant to reduce.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one short paragraph (3 sentences) distinguishing 'guideline as recommendation' from 'guideline as default', at least one 5+ sentence paragraph on why requiring departure documentation is often more effective than writing better guidelines, at least one one-sentence punch line about what the range of prescribing rates for the same eligible population reveals about unexamined departure
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks scene-then-rule rhythm to present a brief population-health framing: guidelines raise the floor, not the ceiling, and that is why they matter — the top quartile of physicians does not need them; the bottom quartile does
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
